Surah al-Dukhan (The Smoke)

[Meccan, except verse 15. Its verses number 56, 57, or 59.]

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ God knows best what He means by it.
By the Book that makes things clear (al-Kitab al-Mubin), the Qur'an, which makes manifest the lawful from the unlawful.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ It is the Night of Decree (laylat al-Qadr), or the night of the middle of Sha'ban (laylat al-nisf min Sha'ban). In it, it was sent down from the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), from the seventh heaven to the lowest heaven (sama' al-dunya). ﴿Indeed, We have been warners﴾ frightening [mankind] by it.

﴿Therein﴾, that is, on Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) or on the night of the middle of Sha'ban, ﴿is decided﴾, meaning it is distinguished and separated, ﴿every wise matter﴾, meaning every matter that has been made firm, concerning provisions, lifespans and other things that will occur in the year until the same night of the following year.
﴿a command﴾ deciding ﴿from Our presence. Indeed, We have always been sending messengers﴾, the messengers: Muhammad and those before him.
﴿Mercy﴾ — compassion toward those to whom He sent (the messenger) — ﴿from your Lord. Indeed He is the All-Hearing﴾ of their words, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 7:

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾, with "Lord" (rabb) in the nominative as a third predicate (khabar thalith), and in the genitive as an appositive (badal) of "your Lord" (rabbika). ﴿If you are certain﴾, O people of Mecca, ﴿certain﴾ that He, exalted is He, is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, then be certain that Muhammad is His Messenger (ﷺ).
﴿Nay, they are in doubt﴾ about the resurrection, ﴿playing﴾ and mocking you, O Muhammad. So he said: "O Allah, help me against them with seven [years] like the seven [years] of Joseph."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 10:

﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾ Then the earth became barren, and hunger afflicted them severely, until from its severity they saw something like smoke between the sky and the earth.
﴿It covers the people﴾, so they said, ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 12:

﴿Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; indeed, we are believers.﴾ (Meaning: we are believers, affirming Your Prophet.)
﴿How can they have the reminder?﴾ That is, faith will not benefit them when the punishment descends. ﴿And there had already come to them a manifest Messenger﴾ clear in his message.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 14:

﴿Then they turned away from him and said, "Taught, and taken to madness."﴾ That is, "A human is teaching him the Qur'an."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment⁠ — that is, the famine — from you for a little while﴾ [So He removed it from them], ﴿indeed, you will return﴾ [to your disbelief], so they returned to it.
Remember ﴿the Day We shall seize with the greatest seizing﴾: it is the Day of Badr, and al-batsh is seizing with force. ﴿Indeed, We will take vengeance﴾ upon them.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 17:**

﴿And We certainly tested before them the people of Pharaoh﴾, i.e., We tried them (بَلَوْنا), ﴿and there came to them a noble Messenger﴾, who is Moses (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام), ﴿noble﴾ in the sight of Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 18:

﴿أنْ﴾ i.e., by saying ﴿Deliver to me﴾ what I call you to of faith, i.e., show your faith to me, ﴿O servants of God. Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾ concerning what I have been sent with.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 44 (ad-Dukhan), verse 19:

﴿And do not exalt yourselves⦅ta'lū⦆ over Allah﴾ meaning, do not act arrogantly (tatajabbarū) ﴿against Allah﴾ by abandoning His obedience. ﴿Indeed, I bring you a clear authority⦅sultān⦆﴾ a manifest proof (burhān mubīn) ﴿clear⦆ evident⦆ concerning my messengership, so he threatened him with stoning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 20:

﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me﴾ with stones.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 21:

﴿And if you do not believe me﴾ (i.e., do not confirm me as true), ﴿then leave me alone﴾ (i.e., leave off harming me). But they did not leave him alone.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 44, verse 22:

﴿So he called upon his Lord, [saying]﴾ i.e., that ﴿these are a criminal people﴾, polytheists.

﴿So travel﴾, with the hamza of the verb pronounced either cut (*qat'*, أَسْرِ) or linked (*wasl*, اسْرِ), ﴿with My servants﴾, the Children of Israel (Banu Isra'il), ﴿by night. Indeed you will be pursued﴾, meaning Pharaoh and his people will pursue you.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 44, verse 24:

﴿And leave the sea﴾ once you have crossed it, you and your companions, ﴿motionless﴾ (rahwan), still and parted, ﴿until they enter it﴾, the Copts. ﴿Indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾. So he was reassured by that, and they were drowned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 25:

﴿How many gardens they left behind﴾ (jannat, meaning) orchards, ﴿and springs﴾ flowing.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 26:**

﴿And crops and a noble station﴾ a fine assembly
﴿And luxury﴾ enjoyment, ﴿in which they had been ever jesting﴾ living in ease.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 28:

﴿Kadhalika﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning: the matter is so. ﴿And We made others inherit them﴾, i.e., their wealth. ﴿Other people﴾, i.e., the Children of Israel.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 29:

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾ unlike the believers, for whose death their place of prayer on the earth weeps, and the channel through which their deeds ascend from the heaven. ﴿And they were not given respite﴾, i.e., they were not delayed for repentance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 30:

﴿And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment﴾, namely, the slaughter of their sons and the keeping of their women alive for servitude.

Ṭafsīr al-Jalālayn: commentary on Sūrah 44, verse 31

﴿from Pharaoh﴾. It is said it is a substitute (badal) for "the punishment," with an implied noun, meaning "a punishment from Pharaoh." It is also said it is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of "the punishment."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 32:

﴿And We certainly chose them﴾, i.e., the Children of Israel, ﴿with knowledge﴾ from Us of their condition, ﴿over the worlds﴾, i.e., the worlds of their time, meaning the rational beings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 33:

﴿And We gave them of the signs that which contained a manifest trial﴾ a clear favour: the splitting of the sea, the manna and the quails, and other things.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 34:

﴿Indeed, these﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah

﴿It is not﴾ the death after which there is life, ﴿except our first death﴾, meaning when they were drops of semen (nutfah, a drop of seminal fluid). ﴿And we will not be raised again﴾, meaning sent back alive after the second.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 36:

﴿Then bring us our fathers﴾ alive ﴿if you are truthful﴾ that we will be resurrected after our death, i.e., that we will be brought back to life.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 44, verse 37:

﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba'?﴾ (He is a prophet or a righteous man.) ﴿And those before them?﴾ (Of the nations.) ﴿We destroyed them﴾ because of their disbelief. The meaning is: they were not stronger than them, and they were destroyed.

﴿وما خَلَقْنا السَّمَوات والأَرْض وما بَيْنهما لاعِبِينَ﴾ "Playing" (lā'ibīn) is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state in which the act occurs), and the gloss means: "by creating that," i.e., [We did not create them] while playing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 39:

﴿We did not create them﴾ (the two, i.e., the heavens and the earth) and what is between them ﴿except with truth﴾, meaning, creating them with purpose, so that they might serve as evidence of Our power and Our oneness and other than that. ﴿But most of them﴾, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca,

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision﴾ is the Day of Resurrection, on which Allah will judge between the servants. ﴿Their appointed time, all of them﴾ is for the everlasting punishment.

﴿On a Day when no client (mawla) will avail another client at all﴾ by kinship or friendship; that is, he will not ward off anything from him. ﴿A Day﴾ is in apposition to "the Day of Decision." ﴿Anything﴾ of the punishment. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, that is, they will be prevented from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 42:

﴿Except those on whom Allah has mercy﴾: they are the believers, for they will intercede for one another by the permission of Allah. ﴿Indeed, He is the Almighty﴾: the Overpowering in His retribution against the disbelievers, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ toward the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 43:

﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum﴾ is among the most wicked of bitter trees in Tihamah, which Allah the Exalted causes to grow in the Blazing Fire.
"The food of the sinner" (ṭaʿām al-athīm): the food of Abū Jahl and his companions, those possessed of great sin.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn, on Surah 44, verse 45:

﴿Like molten brass﴾, i.e., like the dregs of black olive oil, a second predicate (khabar thani). ﴿Boiling in the bellies﴾, with the feminine-form verb (bil-fawqaniyya, i.e., with the ta' at the start, yaghli read in the second person form) a third predicate (khabar thalith), and with the masculine-form verb (bil-tahtaniyya, i.e., with the yaa') it is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to al-muhl.
﴿Like the boiling of scalding water.﴾ The water that is extremely hot.

﴿Seize him﴾ is said to the Zabaniyah (the angels appointed to punish the damned): Seize the sinner. ﴿Drag him﴾ is read with the ta' vowelled either with a kasra or a damma (فاعْتِلُوهُ), meaning: drag him harshly and forcefully. ﴿Into the midst of Hellfire﴾ means into the middle of the fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 48:

﴿Then pour over his head the torment of the boiling water.﴾ That is, from the boiling water which the torment never leaves, so this is more emphatic than what is in the verse "Boiling water will be poured over their heads." ﴿﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 49:

And it will be said to him, ﴿Taste!﴾ That is, the punishment, ﴿Indeed you were the mighty, the noble.﴾ According to your claim and your saying: there is none between its two mountains (i.e., Mecca) more mighty or nobler than me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 50:

﴿Indeed, this﴾ — the punishment that you see — ﴿is that about which you used to doubt﴾ — you used to be skeptical of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 51:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in a station﴾ a gathering ﴿secure﴾ where fear is kept safe from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 52:

﴿in gardens﴾ — gardens (basātīn)

Qur'anic quotations are kept with markers and translated plainly.

﴿They will wear fine green silk and thick brocade﴾, meaning what is thin of the silk brocade (dībāj) and what is thick of it. ﴿Facing one another﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl): none of them looks at the back of another's neck, because the couches (asirrah) turn them about.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 54:

﴿Thus it is﴾; the matter is to be understood as supplied before it. ﴿And We will marry them﴾ to (ʾtazwīj) or pair them with ﴿maidens with large, lovely eyes﴾, meaning women who are white, wide-eyed, and beautiful.
﴿They call for﴾ seeking the servants, ﴿therein﴾, meaning in Paradise, that they bring ﴿every fruit﴾ from it, ﴿secure﴾ from its ending and its harm, and from every frightening thing.

I need to translate the passage, but first a note: the text is from Tafsir al-Jalalayn, and I'll render it faithfully.

﴿They shall not taste death therein, except the first death﴾ — i.e., the one that was in the world, after their life therein. Some of them said: "illa" (except) here carries the meaning of "ba'd" (after).

﴿Fadlan﴾ is a *maṣdar* (مَصْدَر, verbal noun) in the sense of *tafaḍḍulan* (تَفَضُّلًا), meaning "as a bounty." It is in the accusative case (*manṣūb*, مَنصُوب) and is governed by an implied verb, *tafaḍḍul* (تَفَضُّلٍ), which is understood though not stated (*muqaddaran*, مُقَدَّرًا).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 44, verse 58:

﴿So indeed, We have made it easy﴾ We made the Qur'an easy ﴿in your tongue﴾ in your language, so that the Arabs might understand it from you ﴿so that they may be reminded﴾ they may take heed and thereby believe, but they do not believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 44, verse 59:

﴿So wait﴾ await their destruction. ﴿Indeed, they are waiting﴾ for your destruction. And this was before the command to fight them was revealed.
